headline: High-risk default interaction: Open Interpreter can read/write the shared filesystem and execute shell commands, so it can ingest or overwrite Cognee outputs and propagate errors or leaks.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Cognee can expose documents, workflows, and support history, while Open Interpreter reads the filesystem and clipboard by default. If Cognee writes untrusted content into a shared workspace, Open Interpreter may treat it as instructions. The pair has a direct file/clipboard bridge, so prompt injection is plausible without extra assumptions.
conditions: IF Cognee exports user-controlled text into a filesystem location Open Interpreter reads
IF Open Interpreter is run with clipboard or file-based ingestion of Cognee output
mitigations: Store Cognee outputs in a dedicated read-only directory
Disable clipboard-based ingestion in Open Interpreter
Add a manual review step before any Open Interpreter action
Use separate OS users or containers for the two agents
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to Cognee outputs and reject untrusted instructions

B_data_leakage.rationale: Cognee touches personal data, finance data, and support history. Open Interpreter has broad filesystem access and broad network egress, so any shared workspace can move sensitive files into an external model provider or other network destination. That creates a realistic exfiltration path in default use, with no built-in isolation between the pair.
conditions: IF Cognee stores personal or finance data in a directory Open Interpreter can read
IF Open Interpreter sends file contents or context to a configured model provider
mitigations: Keep sensitive Cognee data outside Open Interpreter's readable paths
Run Open Interpreter with network disabled for sensitive sessions
Use a separate OS account for each agent
Rotate any model-provider keys used by Open Interpreter
requires-engineering: enforce per-directory access controls and DLP scanning

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Cognee supports multiple instances with session memory and agentic user/tenant isolation, but Open Interpreter shares state via filesystem and can write and modify git state. Both can write to overlapping local resources, so concurrent runs can clobber files or repository state. The conflict is especially strong because Open Interpreter has unrestricted local write capability and Cognee is not isolated at the OS level.
conditions: IF both agents target the same directory or git repository
IF Cognee persists session artifacts that Open Interpreter also edits
mitigations: Assign each agent a separate working directory
Pause one agent before the other writes to shared files
Use git worktrees or branches per agent
Back up the repository before automation runs
requires-engineering: add file locks around shared mutable resources

D_cascading_error.rationale: Cognee can generate decisions, workflows, and schema structures, and Open Interpreter can execute shell commands and modify files based on those outputs. If Open Interpreter treats Cognee output as authoritative, a mistaken or manipulated recommendation can cascade into real actions, including code changes or system commands. The pair lacks a documented verification barrier in the profiles.
conditions: IF Open Interpreter consumes Cognee-generated plans without human verification
IF Cognee output is used to drive shell commands or git commits
mitigations: Require human approval before execution
Compare Cognee output against a second source
Restrict Open Interpreter to dry-run mode
Log every command and diff for review
requires-engineering: add schema validation for Cognee outputs before action

E_compliance.rationale: Cognee explicitly touches personal data, finance data, and support history, while Open Interpreter can access the entire local machine and transmit data over broad egress. That combination can create residency or retention mismatches if regulated data is processed locally and then forwarded externally. The profiles do not show a specific certification mismatch, so medium is the highest supportable level.
conditions: IF regulated personal or finance data is processed by Cognee and then forwarded by Open Interpreter
IF retention or residency rules apply to the same dataset in both agents
mitigations: Classify regulated datasets before use
Exclude regulated data from Open Interpreter sessions
Document retention and residency boundaries
Use separate storage for compliance-sensitive records
requires-engineering: implement policy-based routing and retention controls
